key_catalyst: Brent crude briefly above $90 on the ninth consecutive day of U.S. strikes on Iran, lifting September Fed hike odds to ~53% and pressuring long-duration tech
reasoning: Today's decline was a modest, orderly -0.54% fade driven by a late reversal in AI semis and Brent's push above $90 on the ninth day of U.S.-Iran strikes — both continuations of themes the index has been digesting since 2026-07-14, when oil above $86 and Hormuz headlines carried only impact 1-4 against a cooling-CPI rally. The genuinely binary risk this week is Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel, but those prints land Wednesday and Thursday, not tonight, so the pre-earnings de-risking already observed today is not an overnight gap catalyst. Diplomatic channels with Iran remain open per glm-5.2, and semis attracted real bargain-hunting bids intraday (Western Digital, Seagate, Micron, SanDisk +4-6%) before fading, which points to two-way flow rather than one-directional liquidation.
